name: small business loan declined
ig_caption:
A small business loan declined after two profitable years feels personal. It usually isn't. Marcus runs a food truck in Portland: 24 months of profit, $60,000 requested, declined.

He brought his profit and loss statement. The loan officer wanted the other page, the balance sheet.

A P&L is a movie of your year. A balance sheet is a photo of one day. Lenders fund position, not performance.

The whole balance sheet is one rule:
Assets = Liabilities + Equity
What you own. What you owe. What's left for you.

The three numbers a lender checks, in order:
→ Current ratio: can you cover short-term bills? (Marcus: 1.6)
→ Debt-to-equity: how much is borrowed? (Marcus: 2.8)
→ Retained earnings: what have you kept in the business? ($9,400)

Marcus missed on exactly one, the second. He paid down a truck loan, waited a quarter, and was approved on the same revenue.
